formation.title: The Birth of Belgium
formation.text:
The revolution has succeeded. From the opera house in Brussels to the barricades of the September Days, the people of the southern provinces have thrown off the yoke of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands. Now a new nation takes shape, one that must forge its own identity from the Flemish cloth halls of Ghent, the Walloon forges of Liege, and the cosmopolitan salons of Brussels.

The great powers watch with interest. Belgium sits at the crossroads of Europe, and the path it chooses now will determine whether this small nation becomes a workshop of industry or a haven of diplomacy and peace.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Fire the furnaces: Belgium shall be the forge of Europe!

modifiers.name: Workshop of the World
modifiers.text: Belgium's coal seams, iron foundries, and machine works have made it the industrial engine of continental Europe. From the Sillon Industriel to the textile mills of Ghent, Belgian manufacturing leads the way into the modern age.

options.text: Let the treaty be our shield and compromise our strength.

modifiers.name: Scrap of Paper, Shield of Nations
modifiers.text: The great powers have guaranteed Belgian neutrality by treaty. This small state at the crossroads of Europe survives not by force of arms but by the force of international law, diplomatic skill, and the quiet prosperity that peace brings.

advances.name: Flemish Cloth Halls
advances.text: The great Lakenhallen of Ypres, Bruges, and Ghent where Flemish cloth was inspected, graded, and sold to merchants from across Europe.

advances.name: Bruges Banking
advances.text: The financial innovations of Bruges, where Italian merchant-bankers established the first bourse and pioneered instruments of international trade finance.

advances.name: Burgundian Tapestries
advances.text: The tapestry workshops of Brussels, Tournai, and Arras that produced the finest woven artworks in Europe, adorning the courts of kings from Paris to Rome.

advances.name: Flemish Primitives
advances.text: The revolutionary school of Netherlandish painters (Van Eyck, Van der Weyden, Memling) who perfected oil painting and transformed European art.

event.title: The Flemish Primitives
event.text:
A revolution in painting has emerged from the workshops of Flanders. Jan van Eyck, working at the Burgundian court in Bruges, has perfected the technique of oil painting, achieving a luminosity and detail that astonishes all who see his work. His Ghent Altarpiece, completed in 1432, is hailed as the greatest painting in Europe.

Rogier van der Weyden in Brussels, Hans Memling in Bruges, and Hugo van der Goes in Ghent continue the tradition, establishing the Low Countries as the artistic center of northern Europe. Italian masters cross the Alps to study their techniques.

options.text: Let the world marvel at Flemish mastery.

advances.name: Walloon Guards Tradition
advances.text: The tradition of elite Catholic infantry recruited from Wallonia, serving as professional soldiers in the armies of Spain and later forming the backbone of Belgian military identity.

advances.name: Antwerp Bourse
advances.text: The world's first purpose-built commodities exchange, established in Antwerp in 1531, where merchants of all nations traded goods, futures, and bills of exchange.

event.title: The Antwerp Bourse
event.text:
In 1531, a magnificent new building opened its doors in Antwerp, the world's first purpose-built commodities exchange. Here, merchants from across Europe gather to trade not just goods but futures, options, and bills of exchange. The Bourse has transformed Antwerp from a mere port into the financial capital of the continent, where the price of pepper from the Indies and silver from the Americas is set daily.

The inscription above its entrance reads: 'For the use of merchants of all nations and all languages', a fitting motto for a city that welcomes the world.

advances.name: Plantin Press
advances.text: Christophe Plantin's printing house in Antwerp became the largest in Europe, publishing the Polyglot Bible and establishing the Low Countries as a center of book production.

advances.name: Fortified Cities
advances.text: The fortified urban centers of the Southern Netherlands (Antwerp, Brussels, Ghent, Namur) whose walls and bastions made them formidable strongholds.

advances.name: Liege Arms Industry
advances.text:
The weapons manufactories of Liege and its surroundings, producing firearms, edged weapons, and armor of renowned quality for armies across Europe.

Available in: Liege Armory

advances.name: Abbey Brewing Tradition
advances.text: The monastic brewing traditions of Belgium's Trappist and abbey breweries, where monks perfected the art of ale-making over centuries.

advances.name: Brussels Lace Industry
advances.text: The delicate needle and bobbin lace of Brussels, Bruges, and Mechelen, luxury textiles prized in the courts of Europe.

advances.name: Collateral Councils
advances.text: The Council of State, Privy Council, and Council of Finance that governed the Southern Netherlands under Habsburg rule, providing administrative continuity.

advances.name: Antwerp Diamond Exchange
advances.text:
Antwerp's diamond cutting quarter, where skilled craftsmen transformed rough stones into brilliant gems, making the city the world capital of the diamond trade.

Available in: Diamantwijk

advances.name: Cockerill Ironworks
advances.text: John Cockerill's integrated manufacturing complex at Seraing near Liege, the largest ironworks on the European continent, producing steam engines, rails, and machinery.

advances.name: Sillon Industriel
advances.text: The industrial corridor along the Sambre-Meuse valley from Mons to Liege, where coal mining, steelmaking, and machine manufacturing transformed Belgium into the first industrialized country on the continent.

event.title: The Sillon Industriel
event.text:
The Sambre-Meuse river valley has been transformed. From Mons to Liege, the old agricultural landscape has given way to a continuous corridor of coal pits, blast furnaces, machine shops, and railway lines. John Cockerill's integrated ironworks at Seraing has become the largest manufacturing complex on the continent, producing everything from steam engines to iron rails.

Belgium is now the first country on the European mainland to fully industrialize, and the Sillon Industriel, the 'Industrial Furrow', stands as living proof that the age of coal and steel has arrived.

options.text: The furnaces shall never go cold.

modifiers.name: Industrial Momentum
modifiers.text: The coal mines of the Borinage and the blast furnaces of Liege have transformed the Sambre-Meuse valley into a corridor of smoke, steel, and relentless production.

advances.name: Civic Guard Tradition
advances.text: The Garde Civique, the citizen militia that defended the Belgian Revolution and maintained order in the new state, drawing on the ancient tradition of urban militias in the Low Countries.

advances.name: Canal Infrastructure
advances.text: The canal network linking the Scheldt, Meuse, and Rhine river systems, enabling cheap transport of coal, steel, and manufactured goods across the Low Countries.

advances.name: Verviers Wool Industry
advances.text:
The mechanized wool processing industry of Verviers, where William Cockerill installed the first spinning machines on the continent, transforming artisan workshops into modern factories.

Available in: Tapisserie

advances.name: Constitution of 1831
advances.text: One of the most liberal constitutions in Europe, establishing freedom of the press, freedom of association, and a constitutional monarchy where sovereignty rests with the people.

event.title: The Belgian Constitution
event.text:
On February 7, 1831, the National Congress adopted what would become one of the most progressive constitutions in Europe. It established a constitutional monarchy with broad guarantees of individual liberties, freedom of the press, freedom of association, freedom of worship, and freedom of education. The title 'King of the Belgians' rather than 'King of Belgium' was a deliberate choice, emphasizing that sovereignty rested with the people, not the crown.

The Belgian model would inspire constitutional reformers across the continent for decades to come, proving that a diverse nation could govern itself through law rather than force.

options.text: A constitution worthy of a free people.

modifiers.name: Spirit of the Constitution
modifiers.text: The Belgian Constitution of 1831 stands as a model of liberal governance, protecting individual freedoms while binding together two linguistic communities under a constitutional monarchy.

advances.name: Chasseurs Ardennais
advances.text: Elite light infantry specialists of the Ardennes forests and hills, known for their tenacity, fieldcraft, and the green beret with wild boar insignia.

advances.name: Continental Railways
advances.text: Belgium's pioneering railway network, the first on the European continent, connecting Brussels to Mechelen in 1835 and rapidly expanding to link all major industrial centers.

advances.name: National Bank
advances.text: The National Bank of Belgium, established to provide financial stability, manage currency, and support the credit needs of the new industrial economy.

advances.name: Walloon Steelworks
advances.text:
The mature steel industry of Wallonia, where the Bessemer process and open-hearth furnaces produce the structural steel that builds railways, bridges, and factories across Europe.

Available in: Cockerillsmelterij

advances.name: Linguistic Compromise
advances.text: The pragmatic accommodation between Flemish and Walloon communities, recognizing that Belgium's strength lies in unity through diversity rather than forced assimilation.

destiny.name: Belgian Destiny
destiny.text: Belgium has been forged from revolution. The path forward begins with stable governance, only then can the nation pursue its chosen destiny.

event.title: A Destiny Forged
event.text:
Belgium stands. Born from revolution, bound by constitution, this small nation at the crossroads of Europe has proven that it can endure. The great powers may have guaranteed our borders, but it is we who must decide what kind of nation we shall become.

The path ahead is ours to choose.

destiny.name: The Forge Belt
destiny.text: Secure the industrial borderlands. Aachen's coal and Cambrai's forges must fall under Belgian control to fuel the workshop of the world.

event.title: The Forge Belt Secured
event.text:
The borderlands have fallen into Belgian hands. Aachen's workshops and Cambrai's forges now serve Belgian industry. The coal and iron of the frontier feed a growing appetite for steel, and the blast furnaces burn day and night.

This is just the beginning. Greater prizes lie beyond, the vast coalfields of the Ruhr await.

options.text: The furnaces shall never go cold.

destiny.name: The Ruhr Corridor
destiny.text: Extend Belgian industrial dominion into the Westphalian coalfields. Essen's furnaces shall feed Belgian ambition, and Liège, the forge on the Meuse, must grow to match the scale of this enterprise.

conditions.text: We own Liège and its development is at least 36

event.title: The Ruhr Corridor
event.text:
Belgian industry now extends deep into the Westphalian coalfields. The integration of Ruhr coal with Belgian steel has created an industrial complex without equal on the continent. Liège has grown into a city of furnaces along the Meuse, smoke rises from a thousand chimneys, and the railway links grow thicker by the month.

But power of this scale demands choices. Shall we protect our industries behind tariff walls, or shall we let the coal barons reshape our society as they see fit?

options.text: Raise the tariffs: protect Belgian industry!

modifiers.name: Industrial Expansion
modifiers.text: Belgian industry expands along the coal seams and river valleys, protected by tariff walls and sustained by cheap labor.

options.text: Let the industrialists build their empires.

modifiers.name: Coal Barons
modifiers.text: The captains of industry wield enormous influence, channeling profits from the mines into commercial ventures while the workers bear the cost of industrial disruption.

destiny.name: Continental Forge
destiny.text: From the Meuse to the Rhine, from Flanders to the Seine, Belgium commands the industrial heart of Europe. Cologne and Paris acknowledge Belgian supremacy.

event.title: The Continental Forge
event.text:
From the spires of Cologne to the boulevards of Paris, Belgium commands the industrial heart of Europe. The great cities of the continent acknowledge what the coal barons and steel magnates always knew, that the nation that controls the forge controls the future.

Belgian arms and Belgian steel have built an empire of industry. Shall we forge iron discipline to defend it, or shall we become the arsenal that arms all of Europe?

modifiers.name: Iron Discipline
modifiers.text: Belgian arms and Belgian discipline are the envy of Europe. The industrial forge has been turned to military purpose, though the relentless focus on martial strength comes at a cost to softer pursuits.

options.text: Let Belgian arms supply the continent.

modifiers.name: Arsenal of Europe
modifiers.text: From the armories of Liege to the foundries of the Ruhr, Belgian weapons arm half the continent. The homeland is a fortress, though industrial complacency threatens innovation.

destiny.name: The Treaty Shield
destiny.text: Behind the shield of guaranteed neutrality, Belgium prospers. Build Antwerp, the city of the first Bourse, up to a quarter more than it was, and accumulate the wealth that makes a small state indispensable.

conditions.text: Chose Scrap of Paper, Shield of Nations
We own Antwerp and its development is at least 41

event.title: Under the Treaty Shield
event.text:
The treaty of guarantee holds firm. Behind this shield of paper and ink, Belgium prospers in ways that empires cannot. Our banks lend to kings, our merchants trade with all, and our neutrality is the foundation upon which continental peace rests.

Let others wage war. Belgium shall grow rich in peace.

destiny.name: Model Constitution
destiny.text: The Belgian constitution inspires reformers across Europe. Extend your diplomatic influence to The Hague and build Brussels up into a capital worthy of the congress that wrote it.

conditions.text: We own Brussels and its development is at least 46

event.title: The Belgian Model
event.text:
Reformers from Berlin to Buenos Aires study the Belgian constitution, and come to see it at work in a Brussels grown into a true capital. Our separation of powers, our guarantee of individual liberties, our accommodation of linguistic diversity, these innovations have made Belgium a model for nations seeking to govern themselves through law rather than force.

Shall we lean into this role as a beacon of progressive reform, or shall we emphasize the pragmatic compromises that hold our own diverse nation together?

options.text: Let Belgium be a beacon of liberty!

modifiers.name: Beacon of Liberty
modifiers.text: Belgium's liberal constitution and commitment to education and innovation make it a beacon for progressive thinkers, though the pacifist spirit makes war a costlier proposition.

modifiers.name: Pragmatic Compromise
modifiers.text: The Belgian genius for compromise and accommodation holds together a diverse nation and earns the loyalty of its partners through conciliation rather than coercion.

destiny.name: Heart of Europe
destiny.text: Brussels has become the diplomatic capital of the continent. Luxury goods flow through Belgian markets, and the world's statesmen gather in Belgian halls.

event.title: The Heart of Europe
event.text:
Brussels has become what Vienna once was, the diplomatic capital of the continent. In the grand palaces along the Rue de la Loi, ambassadors negotiate, treaties are drafted, and the affairs of nations are settled over Belgian chocolate and Trappist ale.

The world comes to Brussels. Shall we become the permanent congress of nations, or shall we let our merchants transform this diplomatic capital into a commercial one?

options.text: Brussels shall arbitrate the affairs of nations.

modifiers.name: Congress of Nations
modifiers.text: Brussels has become the seat of European diplomacy, where treaties are signed, disputes arbitrated, and the balance of power maintained through Belgian mediation.

options.text: Let commerce be the language of diplomacy.

modifiers.name: Merchant Republic
modifiers.text: Belgian merchants command the crossroads of European trade. The Antwerp exchange sets prices, the Brussels banks set terms, and the port of Ostend connects the continent to the world.

units.name: Walloon Guards
units.text: Elite professional infantry recruited from Catholic Wallonia. Originally raised for Spanish service, these disciplined soldiers are renowned for their steadfastness in battle and loyalty to their commanders.

units.name: Garde Civique
units.text: Armed citizen militia drawn from the urban population. Heirs to the ancient tradition of Low Countries civic militias, the Garde Civique defends the Belgian state with the fervor of those who fought for their own freedom.

units.name: Chasseurs Ardennais
units.text: Elite light infantry of the Ardennes, trained in forest warfare, ambush tactics, and rapid movement through difficult terrain. Their green berets mark them as the 'Green Wolves' of the Belgian army.

buildings.name: Lakenhalle
buildings.text: A grand cloth inspection and trading hall in the Flemish tradition, where textiles are graded for quality and sold to merchants from across Europe.

buildings.name: Tapisserie
buildings.text: A tapestry workshop in the Burgundian tradition, where skilled weavers create magnificent textile artworks from wool, silk, and precious dyes.

buildings.name: Abdijbrouwerij
buildings.text: A monastic brewery where Trappist monks craft distinctive ales using traditional recipes perfected over centuries of contemplative labor.

buildings.name: Drukkerij
buildings.text: A printing workshop in the tradition of Christophe Plantin's Officina, producing books, maps, and pamphlets that spread knowledge across Europe.

buildings.name: Diamantwijk
buildings.text: A diamond cutting and polishing quarter where master craftsmen transform rough stones into brilliant gems, making this the world center of the diamond trade.

buildings.name: Vesting
buildings.text: A star fortress in the Southern Netherlands tradition, with angled bastions and layered defenses designed to withstand siege artillery.

buildings.name: Liege Armory
buildings.text: An arms workshop in the tradition of the Prince-Bishopric of Liege, where skilled gunsmiths produce firearms and weaponry of renowned quality for armies across Europe.

buildings.name: Cockerillsmelterij
buildings.text: An integrated iron foundry and machine works in the style of Cockerill's Seraing complex, producing steel, steam engines, and industrial machinery. It stands on the coal or the iron ore of the Walloon basins and works its own pits.

children.text: The location's raw material is Iron
The location's raw material is Coal

buildings.name: Wapenfabriek
buildings.text: A Belgian national arms factory, combining Liege's gunsmithing tradition with Ruhr steel and industrial-scale manufacturing to produce weapons for the armies of Europe.

buildings.name: Palais des Nations
buildings.text: A grand diplomatic palace where European statesmen gather to negotiate treaties, arbitrate disputes, and conduct the business of nations over Belgian hospitality.

list.name: Joyous Entry of Brabant
list.text: The constitutional charter granted by Duchess Joanna and Duke Wenceslaus on 3 January 1356, binding every successor duke to customary law and requiring the consent of the estates for new taxes and ducal appointments. Sworn afresh by every prince at his Inkomst, the charter enshrined the right of disobedience to unlawful commands and made Brabant the first Low Countries polity to constrain its prince by written law.

list.name: Great Council of Mechelen
list.text: Charles the Bold made Mechelen the seat of the supreme court of the Low Countries in 1473; Philip the Handsome made it permanent in 1504. Sitting in the Schepenhuis, the Great Council heard appeals from every provincial council in the Seventeen Provinces and exercised cassation over local seigneurial courts, binding the realm into a single jurisdiction until the French abolition of 1795.

list.name: Collateral Councils
list.text: Charles V's reform of 1 October 1531 reorganised the central government of the Habsburg Netherlands into three Brussels councils: the Council of State for great affairs of war and dynasty, the Privy Council or Geheime Raad for legal and administrative ordinances, and the Council of Finances. The trio processed the daily business of the Seventeen Provinces under Granvelle, Egmont, Orange and Horne until the regime's collapse in the 1790s.

list.name: Antwerp Bourse
list.text: The world's first purpose-built commodity exchange, opened in 1531 to a Brabantine Gothic design by Domien de Waghemakere. Each foreign merchant nation (Portuguese, Spanish, English, Hanseatic, Florentine) maintained a standing pitch under the colonnade where bills of exchange and Antwerp pepper were quoted alongside English cloth. The model was copied by Gresham's Royal Exchange in London, then by Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Lille and every great trading capital.

list.name: Four Members of Flanders
list.text: The parliament of the Flemish wool economy, formed by Ghent, Bruges, Ypres and the Franc of Bruges. The cloth-hall guilds in each city gave the Members a base of armed weavers and fullers; their refusal of taxation could, and did, bankrupt counts and dukes. By the 1360s guild deans drew civic salaries and sat alongside patricians, making the Members a body in which craftsmen helped shape the laws of their own cities.

list.name: Three Estates of Liège
list.text: The Ruling of 1684 fixed the constitution of the Prince-Bishopric: the prince-bishop was to govern only in agreement with the upper clergy of Saint-Lambert, fifteen named noble families representing the countryside, and the bourgeoisie organised in thirty-two crafts. Mayors and councillors were drawn from sixteen lifetime electoral chambers. The arrangement held until the Liège Revolution of 1789-91 and the French annexation of 1795.

list.name: Société Générale de Belgique
list.text: Founded 1822 by King William I as the Algemeene Maatschappij ter begunstiging der volksvlijt and inherited intact by the new Belgian state in 1830. Under Ferdinand de Meeus the Société Générale pioneered industrial banking on the Continent, financing the coal pits of Hainaut, the iron-works of Liège, and from 1834 the world's second public railway network. With the Banque de Belgique of 1835 it made Brussels the financial capital of early-industrial Europe.
